lessons.title: My school and my subjects
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I talk about the subjects I study in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to name school subjects and say which I study and like
successCriteria: All: name eight school subjects
Most: say what I study and like: أَدْرُسُ ... وَأُحِبُّ ...
Some: give a reason with لِأَنَّ
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE: thinking about strengths and future choices
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: seeking knowledge is an act of worship

hook.text: If you could only study three subjects, which would you choose and why?
hook.a: Any answer with reasons; today we say it in Arabic.

islamicLink.text: Allah taught us the du'a: رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge' (Ta Ha 20:114). Every subject can be studied with this intention.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'I will go': A) سَأَذْهَبُ B) ذَهَبْتُ
Active participle of د ر س?

teach.heading: School subjects
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Spot the sun letters: ar-, at-, ad-.

teach.heading: I study, I like
bullets: أَدْرُسُ العُلُومَ وَالتَّارِيخَ: I study science and history
لَا أُحِبُّ ...: I do not like ...
teach.note: After أَدْرُسُ / أُحِبُّ the subject is the object: fathah (or kasrah for ـَات plurals: الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ).

teach.heading: Giving a reason
teach.note: العُلُوم is a non-human plural, so it is treated as feminine singular: لِأَنَّهَا.

check.q: 'I like history because it is interesting':
check.why: التَّارِيخ is masculine singular: لِأَنَّهُ مُمْتِعٌ.

practice.q: Say: I study Arabic and I like it because it is useful.
practice.a: أَدْرُسُ اللُّغَةَ العَرَبِيَّةَ وَأُحِبُّهَا لِأَنَّهَا مُفِيدَةٌ.
practice.model:
أَدْرُسُ اللُّغَةَ العَرَبِيَّةَ (object).
وَأُحِبُّهَا: 'and I like it' (ـهَا for a feminine noun).
لِأَنَّهَا مُفِيدَةٌ.

independent.q: Core: Write five sentences about the subjects you study, with likes and dislikes.
independent.a: For example: أَدْرُسُ ثَمَانِيَ مَوَادَّ. أُحِبُّ العُلُومَ. أُحِبُّ اللُّغَةَ العَرَبِيَّةَ كَثِيرًا. لَا أُحِبُّ الجُغْرَافِيَا. مَادَّتِي المُفَضَّلَةُ الحَاسُوبُ.
independent.model: Teacher writes two sentences about their own school days.

independent.q: Extend: Add a reason to three sentences with لِأَنَّهُ or لِأَنَّهَا.
independent.a: For example: أُحِبُّ العُلُومَ لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ.

independent.q: Stretch: Say which is your favourite subject: مَادَّتِي المُفَضَّلَةُ ... لِأَنَّ ...
independent.a: For example: مَادَّتِي المُفَضَّلَةُ التَّارِيخُ لِأَنَّ المُعَلِّمَ يَشْرَحُ جَيِّدًا.

exit.q: What does مَادَّة mean? A) subject B) school C) teacher
Big question: say what you study and one subject you like, with a reason.
exit.a: For example: أَدْرُسُ العُلُومَ وَأُحِبُّهَا لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ.

lessons.homework: Write your weekly timetable in Arabic (days and subjects) and mark your favourite subject.
lessons.send: SEND: subject cards with icons (objects only). EAL: subject list with English. Stretch: use أُفَضِّلُ (I prefer) ... عَلَى ....

lessons.title: Giving opinions about subjects with reasons
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I give and justify an opinion in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to give, ask for and justify opinions about school subjects
successCriteria: All: give an opinion with فِي رَأْيِي
Most: compare with أُفَضِّلُ ... عَلَى ...
Some: ask for and answer an opinion question: مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي ...؟
lessons.smsc: Social: disagreeing politely and respecting other views

hook.text: Is it possible for two people to disagree about a subject and both be right? How should we disagree politely?
hook.a: Yes, opinions differ; listen, give reasons, speak kindly.

islamicLink.text: Allah tells us to speak good words to people (al-Baqarah 2:83) and to argue in the best way (an-Nahl 16:125). Giving opinions with reasons, politely, is part of good adab.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'The subjects are useful': A) المَوَادُّ مُفِيدَةٌ B) المَوَادُّ مُفِيدُونَ

teach.heading: Opinion starters
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. After أَنَّ the noun takes fathah: أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ التَّارِيخَ مُفِيدٌ.

teach.heading: Model: a justified opinion

model.problem: Give an opinion about science with a reason.
model.answer: In my opinion science is interesting because we learn about Allah's creation, but it is sometimes hard.

teach.note: Opinion, reason, balancing point: the shape of a strong answer.

teach.heading: Asking for opinions
bullets: مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي العُلُومِ؟: what do you think of science?
أَيُّ مَادَّةٍ تُفَضِّلُ؟: which subject do you prefer?

check.why: أُفَضِّلُ A عَلَى B = I prefer A to B.

practice.a: For example: فِي رَأْيِي الحَاسُوبُ مُفِيدٌ لِأَنَّهُ مُهِمٌّ لِلْمُسْتَقْبَلِ.
practice.model:
Start with فِي رَأْيِي.
Subject + adjective: الحَاسُوبُ مُفِيدٌ.
Reason: لِأَنَّهُ مُهِمٌّ لِلْمُسْتَقْبَلِ.

practice.a: أُفَضِّلُ اللُّغَةَ العَرَبِيَّةَ عَلَى اللُّغَةِ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةِ

practice.q: Ask a girl which subject she prefers.

independent.q: Core: Write opinions on three subjects, each with a reason (portal response box). Starter: فِي رَأْيِي ...
independent.a: For example: فِي رَأْيِي الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ مُهِمَّةٌ لِأَنَّهَا مُفِيدَةٌ فِي الحَيَاةِ. أُفَضِّلُ العُلُومَ عَلَى التَّارِيخِ لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ. أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ الفَنَّ سَهْلٌ.
independent.model: Teacher writes one full opinion with a reason and a balancing point.

independent.q: Extend: In a breakout pair, ask each other مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي ...؟ about two subjects and note the answers.
independent.a: Two questions and two justified answers each

independent.q: Stretch: Write a balanced opinion: positive, negative and conclusion.
independent.a: For example: التَّارِيخُ مُمْتِعٌ، لٰكِنَّ فِيهِ تَوَارِيخَ كَثِيرَةً، وَمَعَ ذٰلِكَ أُحِبُّهُ.

exit.q: What does أُفَضِّلُ mean? A) I prefer B) I study C) I think
Big question: give and justify one opinion in Arabic.
exit.a: For example: فِي رَأْيِي العُلُومُ مُمْتِعَةٌ لِأَنَّنَا نَتَعَلَّمُ عَنِ الطَّبِيعَةِ.

lessons.homework: Ask two family members their opinion of a school subject in Arabic (or translate for them) and write their answers.
lessons.send: SEND: opinion frame: فِي رَأْيِي ___ ___ لِأَنَّ ___. EAL: phrase card with English. Stretch: use أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ with correct fathah.

lessons.title: Sound and broken plurals
lessons.bigQuestion: In English 'man' becomes 'men', not 'mans'. Does Arabic have 'irregular' plurals too?
objectives: To understand the difference between sound and broken plurals and use common ones
successCriteria: All: make sound plurals with ـَاتٌ and ـُونَ
Most: recognise common broken plurals
Some: use plurals with correct adjective agreement

keywords.def: broken plural: the word changes inside

hook.text: In English 'man' becomes 'men', not 'mans'. Does Arabic have 'irregular' plurals too?
hook.a: Yes, many: broken plurals like كِتَاب → كُتُب.

teach.heading: Agreement reminder
bullets: Things in the plural take feminine singular

practice.q: Make plural and describe: the ship is big.
practice.model: Teacher: سَفِينَة → سُفُن (broken). Ships are things, so adjective is feminine singular: السُّفُنُ كَبِيرَةٌ.

independent.q: Plural sort and sentences on the pupil PDF: sort twelve words into sound or broken and write their plurals; then write four plural sentences with correct agreement.
independent.a: Correct sort and plurals; agreement correct
independent.model: Teacher sorts كِتَاب (broken: كُتُب) and مُهَنْدِس (sound: مُهَنْدِسُونَ).

independent.q: Extend: find three broken plurals in a mushaf page (with the teacher's list).
independent.a: e.g. أَنْهَار، جِبَال، قُلُوب

exit.q: Sound feminine plural ends in ...
Back to our ponder: does Arabic have irregular plurals?

lessons.title: My school day in the past, present and future
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I talk about yesterday, today and tomorrow at school in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to describe a school day in the past, present and future
successCriteria: All: say one sentence in each time frame
Most: change a verb between past, present and future: ذَهَبْتُ، أَذْهَبُ، سَأَذْهَبُ
Some: use time words and attached pronouns in a three-tense paragraph
lessons.crossCurricular: English: verb tenses and time adverbials
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: reflecting on yesterday and planning tomorrow with in sha' Allah

hook.text: Examiners love answers that use three time frames. Why do you think using past, present and future shows more skill?
hook.a: It shows control of different verb forms and time words, not just one pattern.

islamicLink.text: Allah swears by time: 'By time, mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do good deeds' (al-'Asr 103:1-3). We use our past, present and future well.

teach.heading: One verb, three times
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Past 'I' ends in ـتُ; present 'I' starts with أَ; future adds سَـ.

teach.heading: My online school day
bullets: يَبْدَأُ الدَّرْسُ الأَوَّلُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ

teach.heading: Model: a three-tense paragraph

steps: أَمْسِ دَرَسْتُ العُلُومَ وَكَانَ الدَّرْسُ مُمْتِعًا.
اليَوْمَ أَدْرُسُ العَرَبِيَّةَ وَأُحِبُّهَا لِأَنَّهَا لُغَةُ القُرْآنِ.
غَدًا سَأَكْتُبُ اخْتِبَارَ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.
model.answer: Three sentences, three time frames, one opinion with an attached pronoun

teach.note: كَانَ + accusative: كَانَ الدَّرْسُ مُمْتِعًا (the lesson was interesting). Note أُحِبُّهَا and لِأَنَّهَا agree with العَرَبِيَّة.

check.q: Which sentence is in the future?
check.why: سَـ + present = future: I will write the homework.

practice.q: Make past and future: أُصَلِّي الظُّهْرَ فِي المَسْجِدِ.
practice.a: Past: صَلَّيْتُ الظُّهْرَ فِي المَسْجِدِ. Future: سَأُصَلِّي الظُّهْرَ فِي المَسْجِدِ.
practice.model:
Present: أُصَلِّي.
Past I-form: صَلَّيْتُ.
Future: سَأُصَلِّي.

practice.q: Translate: Yesterday the lesson was long.

independent.q: Core: Write a paragraph about your school day with two sentences in each time frame (portal response box). Starter: أَمْسِ ...
independent.a: For example: أَمْسِ دَرَسْتُ التَّارِيخَ. كَانَ الدَّرْسُ مُمْتِعًا. اليَوْمَ أَدْرُسُ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ. أُحِبُّهَا لٰكِنَّهَا صَعْبَةٌ. غَدًا سَأَدْرُسُ العُلُومَ. سَأَكْتُبُ تَقْرِيرًا، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.
independent.model: Teacher writes the yesterday pair, then pupils continue.

independent.q: Extend: Add one opinion with لِأَنَّهُ or لِأَنَّهَا in each time frame.
independent.a: For example: ... لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ مُفِيدًا.

independent.q: Stretch: Translate: Yesterday I studied science, today I am studying Arabic and tomorrow I will write an essay.
independent.a: أَمْسِ دَرَسْتُ العُلُومَ، وَاليَوْمَ أَدْرُسُ العَرَبِيَّةَ، وَغَدًا سَأَكْتُبُ مَقَالًا.

exit.q: Past 'I' verbs end in: A) ـتُ B) سَـ C) أَـ
Big question: say one sentence about yesterday, today and tomorrow at school.
exit.a: For example: أَمْسِ دَرَسْتُ، اليَوْمَ أَدْرُسُ، غَدًا سَأَدْرُسُ.

lessons.title: The future tense with سَـ and سَوْفَ
objectives: Form the future tense with سَـ or سَوْفَ
Use future time expressions
Say in shā' Allāh when speaking about the future
starter: Say 'yesterday I went to the mosque' in Arabic.
Give the Arabic for 'tomorrow' if you know it.

teach.heading: Building the future
bullets: أَذْهَبُ → سَأَذْهَبُ - sa-adhhabu - I will go
يَدْرُسُ → سَيَدْرُسُ - sa-yadrusu - he will study
نَلْعَبُ → سَنَلْعَبُ - sa-nalʿabu - we will play
سَوْفَ أَذْهَبُ - sawfa adhhabu - I will go
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The rule is simple: add سَـ to the front of the present tense verb (no space) or use سَوْفَ before it with a space. Write the prefix attached in a different colour. Misconception: leaving a space after سَـ. Both forms mean 'will'; سَوْفَ is more formal or more distant.

teach.heading: Future time words
bullets: بَعْدَ غَدٍ - the day after tomorrow
teach.note: Pair time expressions with sentences: غَدًا سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ. Note the tanween on غَدًا. Ask pupils to write three plans for tomorrow in Arabic and read them to a partner.

teach.heading: In shā' Allāh
bullets: غَدًا سَأَزُورُ جَدِّي إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
سَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
In shā' Allāh - if Allah wills
teach.note: Qur'an 18:23–24 teaches us not to say 'I will do this tomorrow' without adding 'if Allah wills'. Explain that it does not mean we do not plan; it means we trust Allah. Say the future sentences with in shā' Allāh at the end. Pupils add it to all their plans.

teach.heading: Questions about the future
bullets: مَاذَا سَتَفْعَلُ غَدًا؟ - mādhā sa-tafʿalu ghadan? - what will you do tomorrow?
هَلْ سَتَذْهَبُ مَعَنَا؟ - hal sa-tadhhabu maʿanā? - will you go with us?
سَأَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ - I will play football
teach.note: Practise questions and answers in pairs. Use -ka/-ki: مَاذَا سَتَفْعَلِينَ؟ for a girl. Notice that the future prefix سَـ attaches to the second-person verbs too: سَتَفْعَلُ.

teach.heading: Negative future: لَنْ
bullets: لَنْ أَذْهَبَ - lan adhhaba - I will not go
لَنْ نَلْعَبَ - lan nalʿaba - we will not play
لَنْ يَدْرُسَ - lan yadrusa - he will not study
teach.note: Teach لَنْ + present verb with a fatḥa ending. Do not explain the full subjunctive mood; call it 'the will-not form'. Pupils practise two sentences. Check that the final vowel is fatḥa, not damma.

practice: Make the future: أَقْرَأُ, نَكْتُبُ, يَذْهَبُونَ.
Say: 'Tomorrow I will visit my grandmother, in shā' Allāh'.
Ask a boy: 'What will you do next week?'
Make negative: سَأَذْهَبُ → I will not go.
independent: Write eight sentences about your plans for next week using سَـ.
Add in shā' Allāh to at least two plans.
Ask a partner four questions about their plans and write down the answers.
exit: Write 'we will play' and 'he will study' in Arabic.
What do you add to the end of a future plan?
lessons.homework: Write ten future sentences about your plans for half term, with in shā' Allāh.
lessons.send: SEND: future strips with colour-coded prefixes. EAL: bilingual time expressions. Stretch: add لَنْ in three negative plans.

lessons.title: Weekend and holiday plans
objectives: Describe weekend and holiday plans
Name activities and places
Give reasons for plans
starter: Make the future: أَلْعَبُ, يَدْرُسُ, نَذْهَبُ.
Say 'tomorrow, in shā' Allāh, I will go'.

teach.heading: Weekend plans
bullets: سَأَزُورُ جَدِّي - sa-azūru jaddī - I will visit my grandfather
سَنَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ - we will play football
سَأَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ - I will read the Qur'an
سَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ - we will go to the mosque
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Ask pupils to say one plan for the weekend. Revise the first-person and first-person-plural future. Notice the vowel on the verbs: سَأَزُورُ, سَنَلْعَبُ. Keep in mind that pupils may live in different time zones, so refer to 'the weekend' generally.

teach.heading: Places to go
teach.note: Show pictures and name places. Reminder: after إِلَى the noun takes kasra: إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ. Ask: where would you go with friends? Where would you go with family? Pupils sort the places into 'with friends' and 'with family'.

teach.heading: Holiday plans
bullets: سَنُسَافِرُ إِلَى مِصْرَ - sa-nusāfiru ilā miṣr - we will travel to Egypt
سَنَبْقَى فِي الْفُنْدُقِ - we will stay in the hotel
سَنَزُورُ الْأَهْرَامَ - we will visit the pyramids
سَأُشَاهِدُ الْبَحْرَ - I will see the sea
teach.note: Teach سَنُسَافِرُ (we will travel). Note that مِصْرَ and similar country names do not take tanween (diptote). Ask pupils to name a country they would like to visit and say why. Avoid assumptions about families' travel plans: say 'if I could'.

teach.heading: Giving reasons
bullets: سَأَذْهَبُ لِأَنَّنِي أُحِبُّ الْبَحْرَ - because I love the sea
سَنَزُورُ جَدِّي لِأَنَّهُ مَرِيضٌ - because he is ill
سَنَلْعَبُ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ لِأَنَّ الْجَوَّ جَمِيلٌ - the weather is nice
teach.note: Use لِأَنَّنِي (because I) as a chunk. Visiting the sick is a sunnah: the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught that a Muslim has the right to be visited when ill (Sahih Bukhari and Muslim). Pupils write one plan with a reason.

teach.heading: Writing about plans
teach.note: Show a checklist and a model paragraph. Pupils plan three sentences. Check that سَـ is attached and the endings are correct. End with in shā' Allāh.

practice: Say three plans for the weekend.
Translate: 'We will go to the library'.
Give a reason: سَأَزُورُ جَدَّتِي لِأَنَّ____.
Ask your partner: 'Where will you go in the holiday?'
independent: Write a paragraph of 70 words about your plans for the holiday.
Include at least four future verbs and two reasons.
Record a one-minute talk about your weekend plans.
exit: Write 'We will travel to Egypt next week, in shā' Allāh'.
Give one reason to visit a relative.
lessons.homework: Write your plans for the next holiday (80 words) with future verbs and reasons.
lessons.send: SEND: planner with picture prompts. EAL: bilingual place names. Stretch: include a contrast: سَأَذْهَبُ ... وَلَكِنْ لَنْ ....

lessons.title: Invitations: accepting and declining politely
objectives: Invite someone to do something
Accept or decline politely with adab
Use أَنْ + present verb
starter: Say 'we will go to the library tomorrow' in Arabic.
Make a negative future: 'I will not go'.
Say 'in shā' Allāh' and what it means.

teach.heading: Inviting
bullets: هَلْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَلْعَبَ مَعَنَا؟ - want to play with us?
هَلْ تُرِيدِينَ أَنْ تَزُورِينَا؟ - to a girl
أَدْعُوكَ إِلَى الْعَشَاءِ - adʿūka ilā l-ʿashā' - I invite you to dinner
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Hospitality is a strong value in Islam. The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught that whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honour his guest (Bukhari and Muslim). Teach the invitation structure: هَلْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ + verb with fatḥa. Note that after أَنْ the verb ends in fatḥa (تَلْعَبَ). For a girl the final ن of the verb drops, so تَزُورِينَ becomes تَزُورِي, and with 'us' we get تَزُورِينَا; present this as a chunk for recognition.

teach.heading: Accepting
bullets: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَةِ - thank you for the invitation
جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا - jazāka llāhu khayran - may Allah reward you
teach.note: Teach polite acceptance. جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا is a common reply to kindness; use -ki for a girl. Pupils practise accepting an invitation and asking for details. Role-play: one invites, one accepts, and they agree on a time.

teach.heading: Declining politely
bullets: مَعَ الْأَسَفِ لَا أَسْتَطِيعُ - maʿa l-asafi lā astaṭīʿu - sorry, I cannot
عِنْدِي دَرْسٌ - ʿindī darsun - I have a lesson
رُبَّمَا فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ الْقَادِمِ - perhaps next week
شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا - thank you very much
teach.note: Show that declining politely includes an apology, a reason and an alternative. Avoid just saying 'no'. Link to adab: the Prophet (peace be upon him) was gentle in speech. Pupils practise two polite refusals.

teach.heading: Complete dialogue
teach.note: Read the dialogue aloud. Gloss: 'Do you want to visit us tomorrow? Thanks for the invitation, with pleasure. We will wait for you at six. In shā' Allāh.' Ask pupils to identify the polite phrases. Pupils then write their own dialogue.

teach.heading: Adab of hospitality
teach.note: Link hospitality to Islamic character. Ask how pupils welcome a guest at home. Ask what they say to a host when leaving. Accept all answers that show kindness. Pupils prepare for the writing task.

practice: Invite a classmate to play football tomorrow.
Accept the invitation with two polite phrases.
Decline politely and give a reason.
Translate: 'Thank you for the invitation, I have a lesson'.
independent: Write a dialogue of eight lines in which you invite a friend and they decline.
Write a second dialogue in which they accept and you agree a time.
Perform one dialogue with a partner and peer-assess politeness.
exit: Write 'Do you want to visit us?' in Arabic.
Give two phrases for declining politely.
lessons.homework: Write an invitation message (50 words) to a friend for a meal, using at least three polite phrases.
lessons.send: SEND: dialogue strips to reorder. EAL: bilingual phrasebank. Stretch: add formal invitations using يَسُرُّنَا أَنْ (we would be pleased to).

lessons.title: Writing about my plans
objectives: Plan and write a paragraph on future plans
Use a range of tenses accurately
Self-edit for common errors
starter: Make the future of: أَلْعَبُ, نَكْتُبُ, يَقْرَأُ.
Say what you will do tomorrow, with in shā' Allāh.

teach.heading: Structure a paragraph
bullets: Middle: plans with سَـ and reasons
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. A good paragraph has an opening, three or four details and a closing. Show how to join ideas with وَ, ثُمَّ and لِأَنَّ. Pupils copy the structure and put in their own content.

teach.heading: Model paragraph
bullets: غَدًا سَأَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا - I will wake early
سَأُصَلِّي الْفَجْرَ ثُمَّ سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ
فِي الْمَسَاءِ سَنَزُورُ جَدِّي - we will visit my grandfather
سَنَأْكُلُ الْعَشَاءَ مَعًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ - we will eat dinner together
teach.note: Read aloud and gloss. Ask pupils to underline all the future verbs and mark each with the subject. Notice that سَنَأْكُلُ has an alif with hamza. Ask: what time words are used?

teach.heading: Expressing hopes
bullets: أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ أَزُورَ مَكَّةَ - I hope to visit Makkah
أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ أَحْفَظَ الْقُرْآنَ - I hope to memorise the Qur'an
أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا - I want to be a doctor
teach.note: Teach أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ + present verb with fatḥa. Use hopes that suit the pupils' ethos: memorising Qur'an, serving parents, studying. Note that مَكَّةَ has fatha (diptote). Pupils write two hopes.

teach.heading: Check and correct
bullets: Is سَـ attached to the verb?
Does the verb match the subject?
teach.note: Show a short text with three mistakes: سَ أَذْهَبُ (space), سَيَذْهَبُ أَنَا (wrong subject), غَدًا ذَهَبْتُ (past with 'tomorrow'). Pupils correct them in pairs. Praise self-correction as part of ihsan.

teach.heading: Final writing task
bullets: Use at least six future verbs
Include two reasons and one hope
teach.note: Set the success criteria on screen. Pupils write for 20 minutes in the independent section. Circulate and offer feedback in the chat or breakout rooms. Remind them to end with in shā' Allāh.

practice: Translate: 'I hope to visit my grandparents'.
independent: Write a plan paragraph (80–100 words) for the next holiday.
Peer-edit a partner's paragraph with the checklist.
Rewrite the final version after feedback.
exit: Write a sentence with أَتَمَنَّى أَنْ.
Write one future plan with a reason.
lessons.homework: Redraft your plan paragraph at home and read it aloud twice.
lessons.send: SEND: paragraph frame with the first sentence of each part. EAL: model paragraph with audio. Stretch: write a second paragraph on someone else's plans using third person.

lessons.title: In the clothes shop: prices and numbers 20 to 100
lessons.bigQuestion: Is the cheapest item always the best buy? What else should a Muslim shopper think about?
objectives: To understand how to ask and give prices with numbers from 20 to 100
successCriteria: All: say the tens from 20 to 100
Most: ask بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟ and answer with بِـ + number
Some: say compound prices like 35 or 72 pounds
lessons.smsc: Moral: wise spending; Social: polite shopping

hook.text: Is the cheapest item always the best buy? What else should a Muslim shopper think about?
hook.a: Quality, need, avoiding waste, and honest dealing: the price is only one part.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who are excessive' (al-A'raf 7:31).

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Because the weather is cold' is ...
Say 'I wear a coat in winter'.

teach.heading: The tens
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Pupils count along. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Compound numbers
bullets: Units first, then وَ, then the tens
teach.note: Like the old English 'five and thirty'.

teach.heading: Asking the price
bullets: بِكَمْ هٰذَا القَمِيصُ؟ How much is this shirt?
After بِـ the tens end in ـِينَ
teach.note: With 20 to 99 the counted noun is singular with ـًا: جُنَيْهًا.

practice.model: Teacher: after بِـ, سِتُّونَ becomes سِتِّينَ; the noun is singular with ـًا: جُنَيْهًا. Together: بِسِتِّينَ جُنَيْهًا.

independent.q: Price tags on the pupil PDF: write ten prices in Arabic words (for example £25, £38, £99), then write four shop exchanges with بِكَمْ ...؟ and the answer.
independent.a: Correct compound numbers and بِـ + ـِينَ forms with جُنَيْهًا
independent.model: Teacher does £38: ثَمَانِيَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ جُنَيْهًا; بِكَمْ هٰذَا الحِذَاءُ؟ بِثَمَانِيَةٍ وَثَلَاثِينَ جُنَيْهًا.

independent.q: Extend: say 'that is expensive' and 'that is cheap'.
independent.a: هٰذَا غَالٍ؛ هٰذَا رَخِيصٌ

exit.q: بِكَمْ؟ asks ...
Back to our ponder: is the cheapest always best?
exit.a: No: quality, need, avoiding waste and honesty matter

lessons.homework: Look at three price tags at home or online and say the prices in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: number line 20 to 100 with Arabic labels. EAL: price frame. Stretch: say prices with pence: وَخَمْسُونَ بِنْسًا.

lessons.bigQuestion: Two coats: one cheaper, one better made. Which is the better choice, and how would you argue it in Arabic?

successCriteria: All: say أَرْخَصُ مِنْ and أَغْلَى مِنْ
Most: form comparatives on the pattern أَفْعَلُ
Some: use the superlative with ال or the construct to choose the best item
lessons.smsc: Moral: wise choices and honest dealing

hook.text: Two coats: one cheaper, one better made. Which is the better choice, and how would you argue it in Arabic?
hook.a: It depends on need and quality: هٰذَا أَغْلَى لٰكِنَّهُ أَفْضَلُ.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. That is the best' (al-Isra' 17:35).

teach.heading: Comparing two items
bullets: The comparative does not change for gender

teach.heading: The best
bullets: Or with ال: هٰذَا هُوَ الأَفْضَلُ

check.q: 'The black shoes are cheaper than the white' is ...

practice.q: Compare two coats: the grey one is warmer than the blue one (دَافِئ → أَدْفَأُ).
practice.model: Teacher: دَافِئ on the أَفْعَلُ pattern is أَدْفَأُ; then مِنْ; then the other item: مِنَ الأَزْرَقِ.

independent.q: Compare and choose in the portal response box: three pairs of items with prices on the pupil PDF; write two comparisons for each pair and say which you would buy and why, using لٰكِنَّ once. Start: ... أَرْخَصُ مِنْ ...
independent.a: Six correct comparisons with مِنْ, three choices with reasons, لٰكِنَّ used correctly

independent.q: Extend: write a superlative sentence about something in your home.
independent.a: For example: هٰذَا أَكْبَرُ كِتَابٍ فِي بَيْتِنَا

exit.q: The comparative pattern is ...
Back to our ponder: cheaper or better?
exit.a: It depends on need and quality; argued with comparatives

lessons.title: Bridge: what does he look like? Describing people
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I describe what someone looks like and what they are like, kindly and accurately?
objectives: To understand how to describe appearance and character with adjectives that agree
successCriteria: All: describe hair and height: لَهُ شَعْرٌ قَصِيرٌ، هُوَ طَوِيلٌ
Most: make adjectives agree for a male and a female
Some: add character and a link word: هِيَ قَصِيرَةٌ لٰكِنَّهَا قَوِيَّةٌ
lessons.crossCurricular: English: descriptive writing with precise adjectives
lessons.smsc: Moral: describing others without mocking; character matters more than looks

hook.text: When you describe a friend, what matters more: what they look like or what they are like? Why?
hook.a: Character matters more; the Prophet ﷺ taught that Allah looks at our hearts and deeds (Sahih Muslim).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'We have certainly created man in the best of forms' (at-Tin 95:4). The Prophet ﷺ taught that Allah does not look at our bodies and forms but at our hearts and deeds (Sahih Muslim). We describe people with respect.

starter.q: Bismillah. Feminine of أَسْوَد? A) سَوْدَاء B) أَسْوَدَة
Say 'my sister is older than me'.

teach.heading: Appearance
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. لَهُ / لَهَا (to him / to her) is how Arabic says 'has' for features. No pictures of people are used; describe in words only.

teach.heading: Character
teach.note: Add ة for a female; the same rule as nationality and colour (except أَفْعَل colours).

model.problem: Describe my uncle in three sentences.
model.answer: My uncle is tall. He has brown hair and a short beard. He is generous and patient.

check.why: Both adjectives agree with هِيَ: ـَة.

practice.q: Describe a woman with long black hair who is patient.
practice.a: لَهَا شَعْرٌ أَسْوَدُ طَوِيلٌ، وَهِيَ صَبُورَةٌ.
practice.model:
Features with لَهَا: لَهَا شَعْرٌ.
Colour then length: أَسْوَدُ طَوِيلٌ (شَعْر is masculine).
Character, feminine: وَهِيَ صَبُورَةٌ.

independent.q: Core: Describe a real or imagined person you admire in four sentences: height, hair, eyes, character (portal response box).
independent.a: For example: جَدِّي قَصِيرٌ. لَهُ شَعْرٌ أَبْيَضُ. لَهُ عَيْنَانِ بُنِّيَّتَانِ. هُوَ كَرِيمٌ وَلَطِيفٌ.
independent.model: Teacher describes an imagined teacher in four sentences, labelling each part.

independent.q: Extend: Rewrite your description for a female (or male) person, changing every agreement.
independent.a: Correct ة endings and لَهَا / هِيَ throughout

independent.q: Stretch: Join two ideas with لٰكِنَّ + pronoun: لٰكِنَّهُ / لٰكِنَّهَا.
independent.a: For example: هِيَ قَصِيرَةٌ لٰكِنَّهَا قَوِيَّةٌ.

exit.q: 'He has' (for features) is: A) لَهُ B) لَهَا C) عِنْدِي
Big question: describe someone kindly in one Arabic sentence.

lessons.homework: Write a five-sentence description of a person you admire (no photo), including at least two character words.

lessons.title: Bridge: the active and passive participle
lessons.bigQuestion: How can one Arabic root give us 'writer' and 'written'?
objectives: To understand how the active participle (اِسْمُ الفَاعِلِ) and passive participle (اِسْمُ المَفْعُولِ) are formed from a root
successCriteria: All: recognise كَاتِب (writer) and مَكْتُوب (written) from ك ت ب
Most: form فَاعِل and مَفْعُول from three new roots
Some: use a participle as an adjective in a sentence: البَابُ مَفْتُوحٌ
lessons.smsc: Cultural: the root system that makes Arabic a language of patterns

keywords.def: passive participle: the thing done to

hook.text: كِتَاب (book), كَاتِب (writer), مَكْتُوب (written), مَكْتَبَة (library). What do these words share, and what does that tell you about Arabic?
hook.a: The root ك ت ب (writing); Arabic builds families of words from roots.

islamicLink.text: The Qur'an describes the Prophet ﷺ as one whom the People of the Book find mentioned, مَكْتُوبًا, written, in their scriptures (al-A'raf 7:157). The same pattern مَفْعُول gives us مَكْتُوب.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'She has' (for features): A) لَهَا B) لَهُ
What is the root of كِتَاب?

teach.heading: Two patterns
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Put the three root letters into the ف ع ل slots.

teach.heading: Model: from root to participles

steps: Active: ف→ش، ع→ر، ل→ب in فَاعِل: شَارِب (drinker)
Passive in مَفْعُول: مَشْرُوب (a drink, drunk)
Use it: المَشْرُوبُ بَارِدٌ (the drink is cold)

teach.note: مَشْرُوب is used every day for 'a drink'.

teach.heading: Participles as adjectives
bullets: البَابُ مَفْتُوحٌ: the door is open
الكُرْسِيُّ مَكْسُورٌ: the chair is broken
الطَّالِبُ جَالِسٌ: the student is sitting
teach.note: Participles take ة for feminine: النَّافِذَةُ مَفْتُوحَةٌ.

check.q: From ف ت ح, which means 'opened'?

teach.heading: Beyond three letters
teach.note: Most able only: forms with مُـ.

practice.q: Make both participles from س ك ن (living).
practice.model:
فَاعِل: سَاكِن.
مَفْعُول: مَسْكُون.
Meaning: a resident; inhabited.

practice.a: The book is written in Arabic.

practice.q: Active participle of ك ت ب?

independent.q: Core: Complete the table for the roots د ر س، ف ت ح، ع ر ف، ح ف ظ: active participle, passive participle, meaning.
independent.a: دَارِس / مَدْرُوس (studier / studied); فَاتِح / مَفْتُوح (opener / open); عَارِف / مَعْرُوف (knower / known, good deed); حَافِظ / مَحْفُوظ (one who memorises, a hafidh / memorised, preserved)
independent.model: Teacher completes د ر س: دَارِس, مَدْرُوس, explaining the slots.

independent.q: Extend: Write three sentences using a passive participle as an adjective.
independent.a: For example: البَابُ مَفْتُوحٌ. الدَّرْسُ مَفْهُومٌ. الكَاتِبُ مَشْهُورٌ.

independent.q: Stretch: Find a word on the مَفْعُول pattern in Surah al-Fatihah.
independent.a: المَغْضُوبِ (those who earned anger) in غَيْرِ المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ

exit.q: What does اِسْمُ الفَاعِلِ name? A) the doer B) the thing done C) the place
Big question: how does one root give 'writer' and 'written'?
exit.a: The root ك ت ب goes into the patterns فَاعِل (كَاتِب) and مَفْعُول (مَكْتُوب).

lessons.homework: Find five words from one root (e.g. ع ل م: عِلْم، عَالِم، مَعْلُوم، مُعَلِّم، تَعْلِيم) and write their meanings.
lessons.send: SEND: root slot card (ف ع ل) to place letters in. EAL: English -er and -ed beside each. Stretch: place nouns on مَفْعَل: مَكْتَب, مَسْجِد.
resources: Tarbiyyah Secondary KS3 Arabic scheme of work, Autumn 1 essentials (bridge): the active and passive participle
Root and pattern table (portal worksheet)
Mushaf for the stretch task

lessons.title: Bridge: my town and giving directions
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I help a visitor find their way in my town in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to name places in a town and give directions with the imperative
successCriteria: All: name six places in a town
Most: give a direction with اِذْهَبْ، اِمْشِ، خُذْ
Some: change the imperative for a female: اِذْهَبِي
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: reading a map and following a route
lessons.smsc: Social: helping strangers and travellers is part of good character

hook.text: A visitor stops you outside the masjid and asks for the library. What exact words would you need to help them?
hook.a: Go straight on, take the first street, turn right, it is on the left.

islamicLink.text: Allah lists the wayfarer, ابْنَ السَّبِيلِ, among those we should help (al-Baqarah 2:177). Giving clear directions is a small act of kindness.

starter.q: Bismillah. Passive participle of ف ت ح: A) مَفْتُوح B) فَاتِح
Say 'on the right' if you know it, or 'masjid' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Places in town
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. مَكْتَبَة is a place of books: root ك ت ب again.

teach.heading: Directions

head: Arabic
English
rows: the masjid is on the right

teach.note: The imperative gives an order or instruction. خُذْ becomes خُذِ before al- to help pronunciation.

teach.heading: Model: a route

model.problem: From the station to the library.

teach.note: Trace it on a simple map on screen.

teach.heading: To a female
teach.note: Add ـِي for a female listener.

practice.q: Direct a boy: go straight on, then turn right.
practice.model:
اِذْهَبْ مُسْتَقِيمًا.
ثُمَّ (then).
اِنْعَطِفْ يَمِينًا.

independent.q: Core: Use the map on the worksheet. Write directions from the masjid to the park and from the station to the hospital.
independent.a: For example: اِذْهَبْ مُسْتَقِيمًا، خُذِ الشَّارِعَ الأَوَّلَ، اِنْعَطِفْ يَمِينًا، الحَدِيقَةُ عَلَى اليَسَارِ.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first route on the shared map, saying each step.

independent.q: Extend: Write three sentences about your own town: فِي مَدِينَتِي ...
independent.a: For example: فِي مَدِينَتِي مَسْجِدٌ كَبِيرٌ وَمَكْتَبَةٌ. المَحَطَّةُ قَرِيبَةٌ مِنْ بَيْتِي.

independent.q: Stretch: Write the directions to a female visitor.
independent.a: اِذْهَبِي مُسْتَقِيمًا، خُذِي الشَّارِعَ الأَوَّلَ، اِنْعَطِفِي يَمِينًا.

exit.q: What does اِذْهَبْ mean? A) go! B) take! C) turn!
Big question: give a visitor a two-step direction in Arabic.
exit.a: For example: اِذْهَبْ مُسْتَقِيمًا ثُمَّ اِنْعَطِفْ يَسَارًا.

lessons.homework: Draw a simple map of your street (places only) and write directions from your home to the nearest masjid or park.
lessons.send: SEND: arrow cards with the direction phrases. EAL: map with English labels too. Stretch: add distances: بَعْدَ مِئَةِ مِتْرٍ (after 100 metres).
resources: Tarbiyyah Secondary KS3 Arabic scheme of work, Autumn 2 essentials (bridge): My town
Portal arabic y10 lesson 32 (directions) as extra reading for the most able
Town map and direction cards (portal worksheet)

lessons.title: Bridge: weather and the future with سَـ and سَوْفَ
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I say what the weather will be like and what I will do?
objectives: To understand how to describe the weather and talk about the future with سَـ and سَوْفَ
successCriteria: All: describe today's weather in two ways
Most: make a present verb future with سَـ or سَوْفَ
Some: link weather and plans: إِذَا كَانَ الجَوُّ مُشْمِسًا سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الحَدِيقَةِ
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: weather forecasts and the seasons
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: saying in sha' Allah about the future

hook.text: When Muslims talk about tomorrow they say 'in sha' Allah'. Why?
hook.a: Because only Allah knows the future; Allah tells us to say it (al-Kahf 18:23-24).

islamicLink.text: Allah tells us: 'Never say of anything, "I will do that tomorrow", except (adding) "if Allah wills"' (al-Kahf 18:23-24). We add إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ to future plans.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Turn right': A) اِنْعَطِفْ يَمِينًا B) اِنْعَطِفْ يَسَارًا
Say 'go straight on' to a girl.

teach.heading: The weather

head: Arabic
English
rows: it is rainy / it is raining

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Look outside and describe today's weather.

teach.heading: The future

right.title: Future
points: سَأَذْهَبُ / سَوْفَ أَذْهَبُ: I will go

teach.note: سَـ joins the verb; سَوْفَ is a separate word, often for further in the future.

teach.heading: Tomorrow's weather
bullets: Tomorrow the weather will be cold
After سَيَكُونُ the adjective ends in -an
teach.note: كَانَ / يَكُونُ makes the describing word accusative: بَارِدًا.

teach.heading: Model: weather and plans

model.problem: If it is sunny, I will go to the park.
steps: إِذَا (if) + كَانَ (was, used for 'is' after if)
model.answer: إِذَا كَانَ الجَوُّ مُشْمِسًا سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الحَدِيقَةِ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.

teach.note: Most able structure; all pupils can copy it as a phrase.

practice.a: سَأَلْعَبُ فِي الحَدِيقَةِ / سَوْفَ أَلْعَبُ فِي الحَدِيقَةِ.
practice.model:
Find the present verb: أَلْعَبُ.
Add سَـ to its front: سَأَلْعَبُ.
Or put سَوْفَ before it: سَوْفَ أَلْعَبُ.

independent.q: Core: Write a forecast for three days (اليَوْم، غَدًا، بَعْدَ غَدٍ) and one plan for each day.
independent.a: For example: اليَوْمَ الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ، سَأَقْرَأُ فِي البَيْتِ. غَدًا سَيَكُونُ الجَوُّ مُشْمِسًا، سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الحَدِيقَةِ. بَعْدَ غَدٍ سَتُمْطِرُ، سَوْفَ أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first day: اليَوْمَ الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ، سَأَقْرَأُ فِي البَيْتِ.

independent.q: Extend: Add إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ to each plan and one sentence with إِذَا.
independent.a: For example: إِذَا كَانَ الجَوُّ مُمْطِرًا سَأَبْقَى فِي البَيْتِ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.

independent.q: Stretch: Compare the weather in Britain and Saudi Arabia in January in two sentences.
independent.a: For example: فِي بِرِيطَانِيَا الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ فِي يَنَايِر، لٰكِنَّهُ أَدْفَأُ فِي السُّعُودِيَّةِ.

exit.q: What does غَدًا mean? A) tomorrow B) today C) yesterday
Big question: say tomorrow's weather and one plan in Arabic.
exit.a: For example: سَيَكُونُ الجَوُّ مُشْمِسًا غَدًا، وَسَأَزُورُ جَدِّي، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.

lessons.homework: Keep a weather diary in Arabic for five days, with one future plan each day.
lessons.send: SEND: weather symbol cards. EAL: weather word mat with English. Stretch: use لَنْ + subjunctive for 'will not': لَنْ أَذْهَبَ.
resources: Tarbiyyah Secondary KS3 Arabic scheme of work, Autumn 2 essentials (bridge): weather and the future
Portal arabic y9 lessons 5 to 8 (future plans) and y10 lesson 34 (weather) as extra reading
Weather diary sheet (portal worksheet)

lessons.title: Describing subjects and teachers: plurals that take the feminine
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do we say المَوَادُّ مُفِيدَةٌ and not مُفِيدُونَ?
objectives: To understand how adjectives agree with non-human plurals and with people when describing school
successCriteria: All: describe a subject with an adjective
Most: describe several subjects with a feminine singular adjective
Some: describe teachers (human plurals) with a plural adjective
lessons.smsc: Moral: respect for teachers and gratitude for learning

hook.text: In Arabic, 'the books are new' is الكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ: the adjective is feminine singular. Why might Arabic treat a group of things like one feminine word?
hook.a: Arabic grammar treats non-human plurals as feminine singular; only people take plural adjectives.

islamicLink.text: Allah raises in rank those who believe and those given knowledge (al-Mujadilah 58:11). We describe our studies and our teachers with respect.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Because it is useful' (for العُلُوم): A) لِأَنَّهَا مُفِيدَةٌ B) لِأَنَّهُ مُفِيدٌ

starter.a: For example: الرِّيَاضِيَّات، العُلُوم، التَّارِيخ، الحَاسُوب

teach.heading: One subject
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Subjects ending in ـَات (riyadiyyat) and non-human plurals (العُلُوم) take a feminine adjective.

teach.heading: Things in the plural
teach.note: Things: feminine singular. People: plural adjective.

model.problem: Describe the subjects and the teachers.
model.answer: I study eight subjects. The subjects are interesting but some are hard. The teachers are kind and patient.

check.why: الدُّرُوس is a non-human plural: feminine singular طَوِيلَةٌ.

practice.q: Say: The exercise books (الدَّفَاتِر) are new.
practice.model:
الدَّفَاتِر: things, not people.
Non-human plural: feminine singular adjective.
جَدِيدَةٌ.

independent.q: Core: Describe five subjects with an adjective each, and the teachers with one plural adjective.
independent.a: For example: الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ صَعْبَةٌ. العُلُومُ مُمْتِعَةٌ. التَّارِيخُ مُفِيدٌ. الحَاسُوبُ سَهْلٌ. اللُّغَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ جَمِيلَةٌ. المُعَلِّمُونَ لُطَفَاءُ.
independent.model: Teacher writes two: الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ صَعْبَةٌ; المُعَلِّمُونَ صَبُورُونَ, explaining each agreement.

independent.q: Extend: Correct the mistakes: الكُتُبُ جَدِيدُونَ. الطَّالِبَاتُ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ.
independent.a: الكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ. الطَّالِبَاتُ مُجْتَهِدَاتٌ.

independent.q: Stretch: Write a short paragraph on your online school: lessons, subjects and teachers (portal response box).
independent.a: For example: مَدْرَسَتِي عَبْرَ الإِنْتَرْنِتِ. الدُّرُوسُ قَصِيرَةٌ وَمُمْتِعَةٌ. المَوَادُّ مُفِيدَةٌ. المُعَلِّمُونَ لُطَفَاءُ.

exit.q: Non-human plurals take: A) a feminine singular adjective B) a masculine plural adjective
Big question: why do we say المَوَادُّ مُفِيدَةٌ?
exit.a: مَوَادّ is a non-human plural, which takes a feminine singular adjective.

lessons.homework: Write six sentences describing your school things (books, pens, lessons) and people (teachers, pupils) with correct agreement.
lessons.send: SEND: two-column card: things / people. EAL: English labels. Stretch: broken plurals of adjectives: لُطَفَاءُ، كِرَامٌ.
resources: Tarbiyyah Secondary KS3 Arabic scheme of work, Spring 1 week 1 (naming and describing school subjects)
Agreement sort and correction sheet (portal worksheet)

lessons.title: Connectives for longer answers
lessons.bigQuestion: How do connectives turn short sentences into a strong Arabic paragraph?
objectives: To understand how connectives link and develop ideas in spoken and written Arabic
successCriteria: All: use وَ، لٰكِنَّ، لِأَنَّ
Most: add أَيْضًا، ثُمَّ، مَعَ ذٰلِكَ
Some: use بِالإِضَافَةِ إِلَى ذٰلِكَ and لِذٰلِكَ in a paragraph
lessons.smsc: Cultural: the eloquence (balaghah) of Arabic prose

hook.text: Read: 'I like science. It is hard. I study it.' Now: 'I like science, but it is hard; therefore I study it every day.' What made the second better?
hook.a: Connectives: but, therefore. They show how ideas link.

islamicLink.text: Allah describes the Qur'an as a Book whose verses are perfected and then explained in detail (Hud 11:1). Clear, linked speech helps others understand.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'In my opinion': A) فِي رَأْيِي B) مَا رَأْيُكَ

teach.heading: Connectives toolkit
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. لٰكِنَّ and لِأَنَّ need a noun or pronoun after them: لٰكِنَّهَا، لِأَنَّهُ.

model.problem: Link: I like science. It is hard. I study it every day.
steps: بِالإِضَافَةِ إِلَى ذٰلِكَ، أَقْرَأُ كُتُبًا عَنِ الفَضَاءِ
model.answer: أُحِبُّ العُلُومَ لٰكِنَّهَا صَعْبَةٌ، لِذٰلِكَ أَدْرُسُهَا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. بِالإِضَافَةِ إِلَى ذٰلِكَ، أَقْرَأُ كُتُبًا عَنِ الفَضَاءِ.

misconception.right: لٰكِنَّهَا صَعْبَةٌ: لٰكِنَّ needs a noun or attached pronoun after it

practice.q: Link with لِذٰلِكَ: الحَاسُوبُ مُفِيدٌ. أَدْرُسُهُ.
practice.model:
First idea: الحَاسُوبُ مُفِيدٌ.
Result connective: لِذٰلِكَ.
Result: أَدْرُسُهُ.

practice.q: Link with لٰكِنَّ: التَّارِيخُ مُمْتِعٌ. هُوَ طَوِيلٌ.

independent.q: Core: Write a paragraph of 5 sentences about your subjects using at least four different connectives (portal response box).
independent.a: For example: أُحِبُّ اللُّغَةَ العَرَبِيَّةَ لِأَنَّهَا لُغَةُ القُرْآنِ. الرِّيَاضِيَّاتُ مُهِمَّةٌ لٰكِنَّهَا صَعْبَةٌ، لِذٰلِكَ أَتَدَرَّبُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. أُحِبُّ العُلُومَ أَيْضًا. بِالإِضَافَةِ إِلَى ذٰلِكَ، أَدْرُسُ الحَاسُوبَ.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first two sentences, circling each connective.

independent.q: Extend: Swap a partner's paragraph in a breakout room and underline every connective; suggest one more.
independent.a: Peer feedback with one EBI (even better if) suggestion

independent.q: Stretch: Rewrite your paragraph for a friend's school ('his/her subjects') with ـهُ / ـهَا.
independent.a: For example: يُحِبُّ أَخِي العُلُومَ لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ، لٰكِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ التَّارِيخَ.

exit.q: 'However' is: A) مَعَ ذٰلِكَ B) لِذٰلِكَ C) ثُمَّ
Big question: how do connectives make a stronger paragraph?
exit.a: They link ideas: adding, contrasting, giving reasons and results.

lessons.homework: Learn the six connectives in the toolkit and use each in one sentence about your week.
lessons.send: SEND: connective cards colour-coded by job. EAL: English equivalents. Stretch: start a sentence with عَلَى الرَّغْمِ مِنْ أَنَّ (although).
resources: Tarbiyyah Secondary KS3 Arabic scheme of work, Spring 1 week 2 (connectives)
Connectives toolkit card (portal worksheet)

lessons.title: An informal email about my school; unit quiz
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I write an informal email that shows everything I have learnt this half term?
objectives: To understand how to structure an informal Arabic email using subjects, opinions, connectives and three time frames
successCriteria: All: write an email with a greeting, three sentences and a sign-off
Most: include opinions with reasons and connectives
Some: use past, present and future in one email
lessons.crossCurricular: English: writing for audience and purpose (informal letters and emails)
lessons.smsc: Social: keeping in touch with friends and family by writing kindly

hook.text: A cousin in another country asks 'What is your new school like?' What would you tell them first?
hook.a: Greeting, that it is online, favourite subjects and why, what you did and will do.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ sent letters to rulers that began with Bismillah (recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari). We begin our letters and emails with Bismillah and salam.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'I will write': A) سَأَكْتُبُ B) كَتَبْتُ

teach.heading: Email structure

timeline.text: بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ; عَزِيزِي أَحْمَدُ / عَزِيزَتِي مَرْيَمُ
My school and subjects, with opinions

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. The school's Arabic intent sets an informal email as this unit's writing assessment.

teach.heading: Model email

quote.text: عَزِيزِي يُوسُفُ، اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ مَدْرَسَتِي الجَدِيدَةُ عَبْرَ الإِنْتَرْنِتِ. أَدْرُسُ ثَمَانِيَ مَوَادَّ، وَمَادَّتِي المُفَضَّلَةُ العُلُومُ لِأَنَّهَا مُمْتِعَةٌ، لٰكِنَّ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ صَعْبَةٌ. أَمْسِ كَتَبْتُ تَقْرِيرًا عَنِ المَاءِ، وَغَدًا سَأَقْرَأُ سُورَةَ المُلْكِ فِي دَرْسِ القُرْآنِ. مَعَ تَحِيَّاتِي، آدَمُ
quote.source: Model email written for this lesson

teach.note: Pupils find: two opinions, two connectives, three time frames.

check.q: How do you begin an email to a girl?

teach.heading: Success checklist
teach.note: Pupils tick the checklist before submitting.

practice.q: Write the opening two lines to a friend called Bilal.
practice.a: عَزِيزِي بِلَالُ، اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟
practice.model:
Dear (m): عَزِيزِي + name.
Salam.
How are you? كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟

independent.q: Core (portal response box): Write an informal email of 60 to 90 words to a cousin about your school: subjects, opinions with reasons, something you did and something you will do.
independent.a: Model as on the slide; assessed on content, range of language (connectives, three time frames) and accuracy (agreement, verb forms).
independent.model: Teacher plans the email aloud with the five-part structure and writes the first two lines.

independent.q: Extend (unit quiz, Forms): 1) 'science' 2) 'in my opinion' 3) feminine plural agreement: المَوَادُّ (مُفِيد) 4) past of أَكْتُبُ (I) 5) 'therefore'.
independent.a: 1) العُلُوم 2) فِي رَأْيِي 3) المَوَادُّ مُفِيدَةٌ 4) كَتَبْتُ 5) لِذٰلِكَ

independent.q: Stretch: Add a sentence comparing two subjects with أَفْعَل مِنْ.
independent.a: For example: العُلُومُ أَصْعَبُ مِنَ التَّارِيخِ.

exit.q: What is بَرِيد إِلِكْتُرُونِيّ? A) email B) letter box C) website
Big question: what did you include in your email to show your learning?

lessons.title: Describing clothes: colour and agreement
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do you think Arabic colour words have their own special pattern?
objectives: To understand how colour adjectives agree with masculine and feminine nouns
successCriteria: All: say six colours in the masculine
Most: give the feminine form of each colour
Some: describe three items with a colour and a second adjective
lessons.smsc: Cultural: dress in Arabic-speaking countries; Spiritual: beauty without pride

hook.text: Why do you think Arabic colour words have their own special pattern?
hook.a: They follow fixed patterns: أَفْعَلُ for masculine and فَعْلَاءُ for feminine, which makes them easy to predict.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah is beautiful and loves beauty' (Muslim), said when a man asked about liking good clothes and shoes.

starter.q: Ask a girl 'what are you wearing?'

teach.heading: Colours, two patterns
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Agreement
bullets: Colours on these patterns take no tanwin
teach.note: The adjective follows the noun and matches its gender.

teach.heading: Two adjectives
bullets: فُسْتَانٌ أَزْرَقُ طَوِيلٌ: a long blue dress
حِذَاءٌ أَسْوَدُ جَدِيدٌ: new black shoes
Colour first, then the other adjective
teach.note: Order is a common style; both must agree.

check.why: Masculine noun, masculine colour, no tanwin on أَخْضَرُ.

practice.model: Teacher: قُبَّعَة ends in ة, so feminine. Red feminine is حَمْرَاءُ. Together: قُبَّعَةٌ حَمْرَاءُ.

independent.q: Describe five items from a clothes shop photo on the pupil PDF with colour and one more adjective; then describe your school uniform or Eid clothes in three sentences in the portal response box.
independent.a: Correct gender agreement and patterns, for example: مِعْطَفٌ رَمَادِيٌّ قَصِيرٌ؛ عَبَاءَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ جَمِيلَةٌ
independent.model: Teacher does item 1: ثَوْبٌ أَبْيَضُ طَوِيلٌ.

independent.q: Extend: what colour is the kiswah of the Ka'bah?
independent.a: أَسْوَدُ: كِسْوَةُ الكَعْبَةِ سَوْدَاءُ

exit.q: Colours in the masculine follow the pattern ...
Back to our ponder: why the special pattern?
exit.a: Fixed patterns: أَفْعَلُ and فَعْلَاءُ, easy to predict

lessons.title: The four seasons and the weather
lessons.bigQuestion: Allah alternates night and day and the seasons. What would life be like with only one season all year?
objectives: To understand how to describe the four seasons and their weather in full sentences
successCriteria: All: name the four seasons
Most: describe the weather in each with يَكُونُ الجَوُّ
Some: compare the weather in the UK and an Arabic-speaking country
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: climates of the UK and the Middle East
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: signs of Allah in the seasons

hook.text: Allah alternates night and day and the seasons. What would life be like with only one season all year?
hook.a: Harder for crops and less varied: the seasons are a sign and a mercy (3:190).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding' (Al 'Imran 3:190).

starter.q: Bismillah. The feminine of أَبْيَضُ is ...

starter.a: أَبْيَضُ، أَسْوَدُ، أَحْمَرُ، أَزْرَقُ، أَخْضَرُ، أَصْفَرُ

teach.heading: Four seasons
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Sentences
bullets: يَكُونُ makes the adjective end in ـًا

check.q: 'In winter the weather is cold' is ...
check.why: يَكُونُ makes the adjective accusative: بَارِدًا.

practice.q: Say: in summer the weather is hot and sunny.
practice.a: فِي الصَّيْفِ يَكُونُ الجَوُّ حَارًّا وَمُشْمِسًا
practice.model: Teacher: فِي الصَّيْفِ + يَكُونُ الجَوُّ + both adjectives in the accusative: حَارًّا وَمُشْمِسًا.

independent.q: Write a weather report in the portal response box comparing the four seasons in the UK and in one Arabic-speaking country, with a temperature for each. Start: فِي بِرِيطَانِيَا ...
independent.a: Eight sentences with يَكُونُ + accusative, temperatures and comparisons
independent.model: Teacher writes: فِي بِرِيطَانِيَا يَكُونُ الشِّتَاءُ بَارِدًا، وَدَرَجَةُ الحَرَارَةِ خَمْسُ دَرَجَاتٍ.

independent.q: Extend: say which season you prefer and why.
independent.a: For example: أُفَضِّلُ الرَّبِيعَ لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ مُعْتَدِلٌ

exit.q: مُشْمِس means ...
Back to our ponder: life with one season?
exit.a: Harder and less varied; seasons are a sign and mercy

lessons.title: What we wear in each season
lessons.bigQuestion: How do you decide what to wear: weather, comfort, modesty or fashion? Which should come first?
objectives: To understand how to say what I wear in each season, with reasons, and talk about modest dress
successCriteria: All: say one item I wear in each season
Most: give a reason with لِأَنَّ
Some: explain in Arabic why modesty matters in clothing
lessons.smsc: Moral: modesty and self-respect

hook.text: How do you decide what to wear: weather, comfort, modesty or fashion? Which should come first?
hook.a: Modesty and comfort first, then weather; fashion only within what pleases Allah.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Haya' (modesty) is a branch of iman' (Bukhari and Muslim).

starter.q: 'In summer the weather is hot' is ...

teach.heading: Season and clothes
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Because ...
bullets: فِي الشِّتَاءِ أَلْبَسُ مِعْطَفًا لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ بَارِدٌ
لِأَنَّ + noun with ـَ: لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ
teach.note: Note the noun after لِأَنَّ takes fathah.

teach.heading: Modesty in dress
bullets: Clothes that cover and are not tight
Haya' is a branch of iman
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim: 'Haya' (modesty) is a branch of iman.' Keep it general and respectful.

check.why: After لِأَنَّ the noun takes fathah; the adjective stays with dammah.

practice.q: Say: in summer I wear a light shirt because the weather is hot.
practice.a: فِي الصَّيْفِ أَلْبَسُ قَمِيصًا خَفِيفًا لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ حَارٌّ
practice.model: Teacher builds it: فِي الصَّيْفِ + أَلْبَسُ + قَمِيصًا خَفِيفًا + لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ حَارٌّ.

independent.q: Write a short paragraph in the portal response box: what you wear in two seasons with reasons, and two sentences on why modest dress matters to Muslims. Start: فِي الشِّتَاءِ أَلْبَسُ ...
independent.a: Correct accusative after أَلْبَسُ, reasons with لِأَنَّ, two sentences on modesty
independent.model: Teacher writes: فِي الشِّتَاءِ أَلْبَسُ مِعْطَفًا دَافِئًا لِأَنَّ الجَوَّ بَارِدٌ.

independent.q: Extend: use لِأَنَّهُ with a clothing item.
independent.a: For example: أُحِبُّ هٰذَا المِعْطَفَ لِأَنَّهُ دَافِئٌ

exit.q: After لِأَنَّ, the noun takes ...
Back to our ponder: what should come first?
exit.a: Modesty and comfort, then weather; fashion within what pleases Allah

lessons.homework: Check tomorrow's weather forecast and say in Arabic what you will wear and why.

lessons.title: Sizes and colours: do you have it in ...?
lessons.bigQuestion: What makes a shopper polite? Which Arabic words would show it?
objectives: To understand how to ask for sizes and colours in a clothes shop politely
successCriteria: All: say small, medium and large
Most: ask هَلْ عِنْدَكَ ...؟ with a size or colour
Some: hold a four-turn shop dialogue with a problem (wrong size)
lessons.smsc: Social: courtesy in shops

hook.text: What makes a shopper polite? Which Arabic words would show it?
hook.a: Greeting, asking kindly and thanking: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، شُكْرًا، جَزَاكَ اللّٰهُ خَيْرًا.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'May Allah have mercy on a man who is easy-going when he buys, when he sells and when he asks for what is owed' (Bukhari).

teach.heading: Sizes
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Polite questions
bullets: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، هَلْ عِنْدَكَ هٰذَا القَمِيصُ بِمَقَاسٍ كَبِيرٍ؟

quote.text:
الزَّبُونُ: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ هٰذَا القَمِيصُ بِمَقَاسٍ مُتَوَسِّطٍ؟
البَائِعُ: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. نَعَمْ، تَفَضَّلْ.
الزَّبُونُ: هٰذَا ضَيِّقٌ قَلِيلًا. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ مَقَاسٌ أَكْبَرُ؟
البَائِعُ: نَعَمْ، هٰذَا مَقَاسٌ كَبِيرٌ.

practice.q: Ask politely for these trousers in black.
practice.a: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، هَلْ عِنْدَكَ هٰذَا البِنْطَالُ بِاللَّوْنِ الأَسْوَدِ؟
practice.model: Teacher: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (please) + هَلْ عِنْدَكَ (do you have) + هٰذَا البِنْطَالُ + بِاللَّوْنِ الأَسْوَدِ (in black, kasrah after بِـ).

independent.q: Role play in breakout pairs: customer and seller, four turns each, asking for a size and a colour and solving a problem (too tight or wrong colour); then write your dialogue on the pupil PDF.
independent.a: Polite greetings, هَلْ عِنْدَكَ ...؟, sizes and colours with agreement, a solved problem
independent.model: Teacher and a pupil perform the first two turns of the model dialogue.

independent.q: Extend: add the price at the end with بِكَمْ ...؟
independent.a: For example: بِكَمْ هٰذَا؟ بِخَمْسَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ جُنَيْهًا

exit.q: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ ...؟ means ...
Back to our ponder: what makes a shopper polite?

lessons.send: SEND: dialogue frame with gaps. EAL: polite phrase card. Stretch: add هٰذَا وَاسِعٌ جِدًّا and ask for a smaller size.

lessons.title: Plurals of clothes
lessons.bigQuestion: English adds -s to most plurals but has 'mice' and 'feet'. Arabic has many 'mice-type' plurals. How can we learn them?
objectives: To understand how clothing words form their plurals, especially broken plurals
successCriteria: All: give the plural of four clothing words
Most: recognise sound and broken plurals
Some: use plural things with a feminine singular adjective
lessons.smsc: Moral: avoiding waste

keywords.def: broken plural: the word's inside changes

hook.text: English adds -s to most plurals but has 'mice' and 'feet'. Arabic has many 'mice-type' plurals. How can we learn them?
hook.a: By learning each word with its plural and spotting common patterns like فَعَالِيل and أَفْعِلَة.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And eat and drink, but be not excessive' (al-A'raf 7:31): buying only what we need.

starter.q: Ask 'do you have it in blue?'

teach.heading: Singular and plural
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

misconception.right: قُمْصَانٌ جَدِيدَةٌ: plural things take a feminine singular adjective

practice.q: Make plural with adjective: فُسْتَانٌ طَوِيلٌ
practice.model: Teacher: plural of فُسْتَان is فَسَاتِين (no tanwin on this pattern). Plural things take a feminine singular adjective: طَوِيلَةٌ.

independent.q: Plural practice on the pupil PDF: give the plurals of ten clothing words with an adjective each; then write a shop window description of five plural items. Start: فِي النَّافِذَةِ ...
independent.a: Correct plurals and feminine singular adjectives, for example: مَعَاطِفُ شَتَوِيَّةٌ؛ أَحْذِيَةٌ سَوْدَاءُ
independent.model: Teacher writes: فِي النَّافِذَةِ قُمْصَانٌ بَيْضَاءُ وَأَحْذِيَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ.

independent.q: Extend: use a number 3 to 10 with a clothing plural.
independent.a: For example: عِنْدِي ثَلَاثَةُ قُمْصَانٍ

exit.q: Plural things take a ... adjective.
Back to our ponder: how can we learn broken plurals?
exit.a: Learn each with its plural; spot patterns

lessons.homework: Make flash cards of ten clothing words with their plurals and test yourself daily.

lessons.title: The imperative in a shop: أَرِنِي، أَعْطِنِي
lessons.bigQuestion: Is a command rude? How can the same request sound polite in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to use the imperative politely in a shop
successCriteria: All: say أَرِنِي and أَعْطِنِي with their meanings
Most: make imperatives from present-tense verbs
Some: soften an imperative with مِنْ فَضْلِكَ and use the feminine form
lessons.smsc: Social: polite requests

keywords.def: the imperative: a command or request
here you are; please (to a boy / girl)

hook.text: Is a command rude? How can the same request sound polite in Arabic?
hook.a: Add مِنْ فَضْلِكَ and a kind tone: أَرِنِي ذٰلِكَ القَمِيصَ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.

islamicLink.text: Ibrahim (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام) said: 'My Lord, show me (أَرِنِي) how You give life to the dead' (al-Baqarah 2:260): the same word, used in du'a.

starter.q: Bismillah. The plural of قَمِيص is ...

teach.heading: Requests in a shop
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

model.problem: Make the imperative of تَكْتُبُ (you write).
steps: Starts with sukun, so add a helping alif: اُكْتُبْ

practice.q: Ask politely: show me the red dress.
practice.model: Teacher: أَرِنِي (show me) + الفُسْتَانَ (object, fathah) + الأَحْمَرَ (agrees) + مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.

independent.q: Shop scene in the portal response box: write six polite requests a customer might make (with أَرِنِي، أَعْطِنِي and two imperatives you form yourself), and the seller's replies with تَفَضَّلْ. Include one request to a female seller.
independent.a: Six correct requests with objects in the accusative, polite softeners, one feminine form
independent.model: Teacher writes: أَعْطِنِي مِعْطَفًا بِمَقَاسٍ كَبِيرٍ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. البَائِعُ: تَفَضَّلْ.

independent.q: Extend: make the imperative of تَذْهَبُ.
independent.a: اِذْهَبْ

exit.q: A polite softener is ...
Back to our ponder: how does a request sound polite?
exit.a: Add مِنْ فَضْلِكَ and a kind tone

lessons.title: Measures and quantities: كِيلُو، لِتْرٌ، نِصْفٌ
lessons.bigQuestion: Allah commands full and honest measure (83:1-3). Why would cheating on weights be so serious?
objectives: To understand and use measures and quantities to buy food
successCriteria: All: say six measures
Most: ask for an amount politely in a shop
Some: use numbers and the construct: كِيلُو تُفَّاحٍ
lessons.smsc: Moral: honesty in trade

hook.text: Allah commands full and honest measure (83:1-3). Why would cheating on weights be so serious?
hook.a: It is stealing from people who trust you; Allah warns those who give short measure.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Woe to those who give less than due, who, when they take a measure from people, take in full, but when they give by measure or weight, give less' (al-Mutaffifin 83:1-3).

teach.heading: The construct: a kilo of ...
teach.note: The second word takes kasrah (tanwin): no 'of' needed.

check.why: Measure first, then the food with kasrah (construct).

practice.q: Say: I want two litres of milk, please.
practice.a: أُرِيدُ لِتْرَيْنِ مِنَ الحَلِيبِ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
practice.model: Teacher: أُرِيدُ + لِتْرَيْنِ (two litres, dual after a verb) + مِنَ الحَلِيبِ + مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.

independent.model: Teacher and a volunteer model the first exchange.

independent.q: Extend: write the dialogue out (six lines).
independent.a: Polite, accurate dialogue

exit.q: نِصْفٌ means ...
Back to our ponder: why is cheating on weights serious?
exit.a: It steals from people who trust you (83:1-3)

hook.a: Most depends on amount: Allah says eat and drink but do not waste (7:31).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And eat and drink, but be not excessive' (al-A'raf 7:31).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge' (Ta-Ha 20:114).

keywords.def: a rice and lamb dish from Jordan

hook.text: Food from every country is different, yet every Muslim says Bismillah before eating. What does that show about the Ummah?
hook.a: Many cultures, one Ummah: the same manners and gratitude everywhere.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Food for two is enough for three, and food for three is enough for four' (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Detailed opinions
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. أُفَضِّلُ ... عَلَى ... = I prefer ... to ...

head: Adjective
Comparative
Example
rows: السَّمَكُ أَكْثَرُ صِحَّةً مِنَ البَطَاطِسِ المَقْلِيَّةِ

practice.q: Say: I prefer fish to meat because it is healthier.
practice.a: أُفَضِّلُ السَّمَكَ عَلَى اللَّحْمِ لِأَنَّهُ أَكْثَرُ صِحَّةً
practice.model: Teacher: أُفَضِّلُ + السَّمَكَ + عَلَى اللَّحْمِ, then the reason with a comparative.
